related_adrs: ADR-0111 (merge queue projected state — serial admission of parallel lanes)
ADR-0196 (SeaweedFS canonical object storage — remote build cache backend)
ADR-0198 (Karpenter node autoscaling — elastic agent capacity)
ADR-0338 (pod runtime tiering — Kata/Cloud-Hypervisor for untrusted CI workloads)
ADR-0346 (oya verify mirrors full CI matrix — lane parity authority)
title: Self-hostable distributed CI farm enabling N-way per-microservice lane parallelism
purpose: Define the canonical distributed CI farm that lets every microservice (vertical lane) build and test in parallel on ephemeral Kubernetes agents, with a shared remote build cache so the 121 kernel + 30 shared-substrate crates compile once and are reused across all lane agents. This is the hyperscaler parallelism enabler: logical parallelism is ~one lane per microservice; physical parallelism scales with elastic agent capacity rather than a single host. Honest-foundation scope: IaC + JCasC + pipeline + cache contract only; no live controller, running agent pool, populated cache, or measured build-farm SLO is claimed.

controller.github_actions_parity: RETIRED per ADR-0361: GitHub Actions removed entirely; cloud-ci is the sole CI. No Actions<->cloud-ci parity is maintained (parity gate dropped). The oya verify CI-mirror (ADR-0346) remains the lane authority.

ephemeral_agents.security: allowPrivilegeEscalation=false; capabilities drop ALL; cosign.sigstore.dev/required=true on agent image
ephemeral_agents.elastic_capacity: Karpenter node autoscaling (ADR-0198) provisions/deprovisions nodes to match concurrent lane demand; cap is a safety ceiling, not a fixed pool.

remote_build_cache.rationale: Bazel-RBE-style shared cache is the primary lever for true N-way parallelism: without it each ephemeral agent recompiles the shared substrate (121 *-kernel + 30 oya-shared-* crates + dependency graph) cold. With it, shared-substrate objects are compiled once and reused across all lanes, so per-lane wall-clock is dominated by the lane's own crates.
remote_build_cache.backend: SeaweedFS S3 API (ADR-0196 canonical object storage; Apache-2.0; self-hostable, license-clean — no external cache dependency)
remote_build_cache.credentials: S3 access/secret bound from OpenBao via the cloud-ci credentials plugin; never inlined in controller config or pipeline definitions.
remote_build_cache.cache_key_discipline: Keyed by rustc version + crate inputs (sccache default) and namespaced by toolchain prefix; cross-lane sharing is safe because cache entries are content-addressed.
remote_build_cache.isolation: Read-write for trunk/dev lanes; pull-request lanes use a read-through view to prevent untrusted PR code poisoning shared entries (write to a PR-scoped prefix, promote on merge).

lane_fanout.logical_lane_model: One lane per microservice vertical (microservices/<ms>/ci/pipeline.yaml). The flat-microservice-catalog + workflow-ontology-adapter-layer architecture invariants guarantee lanes are decoupled (no direct cross-service calls), so lanes run concurrently.
lane_fanout.concurrency_governor: Concurrent lanes are bounded by Karpenter capacity + container_cap, not by a single host; a single dev host realistically sustains ~5-6 heavy lanes, the farm sustains many more.
lane_fanout.shared_library: oya-ci-shared global library carries the cache-wiring and gate-invocation steps so lanes inherit them rather than duplicating.

merge_queue_integration.admission: Parallel lane branches fan in through the ADR-0111 merge-queue projected state; the merge queue serializes admission so concurrent lanes never corrupt trunk.
merge_queue_integration.fan_in_verify: A single serial ./bin/oya verify --ci-required runs the whole-workspace mirror at fan-in; cross-cutting failures route back to the owning lane.
merge_queue_integration.deploy_audit: ArgoCD-driven deploy emits audit-chain rows (ADR-0349 E.5 / ADR-0263).

ci_lane.parity_gate: RETIRED (ADR-0361): no Actions<->cloud-ci parity; cloud-ci is the sole CI
ci_lane.cache_discipline_gate: oya-governance-ci-farm-remote-cache (planned: asserts every microservices/<ms>/ci/pipeline.yaml and the cloud-ci agent templates declare the sccache->SeaweedFS env and do not inline credentials)

deployment.scope: This IS the CI, deployed now on a single local node (colima/k3s). One CI, run locally for now — not a throwaway PoC, and not a separate 'local CI' distinct from production. The only gap to full production posture is SCALE/HA, not a different system.
deployment.iac: infra/ci/ (controller+config+seeds+shared-library, seaweedfs/ S3 cache backend, argocd/ CD + Rollouts, agent-image/ signed image, cache/ warm-cache; deploy-local.sh; README single-node-now vs at-scale deltas)
deployment.evidence: evidence/ci/ — smoke build SUCCESS on ephemeral agent; real build lane (sccache populate -> 100% cross-agent HIT from SeaweedFS); codegen cold/warm measured; Argo Rollouts canary->analysis->promote; ArgoCD GitOps self-heal; SLSA/cosign/SBOM chain proven (syft SBOM + trivy scan + cosign sign + SLSA provenance + CycloneDX SBOM attestations; cosign verify-attestation PASSED).
deployment.realized: cloud-ci controller (config-as-code, numExecutors=0, webSocket agents, non-root UID1000+drop-ALL), ephemeral k8s agents, real repo build lane, sccache->SeaweedFS remote cache (write+hit proven), ArgoCD + Argo Rollouts, cosign-verified SLSA provenance + CycloneDX SBOM.
deployment.scale_deltas: Multi-node Karpenter elasticity (ADR-0198), Kata isolation (ADR-0338), SeaweedFS HA, OpenBao-bound prod creds, and a slim/distroless agent base (trivy found 250 HIGH/CRITICAL in the stock rust base) are the remaining SCALE + hardening deltas. The pipeline + supply-chain stages are identical at scale.

non_claims: No PRODUCTION-SCALE multi-node agent pool or HA is claimed; the CI runs on a single local node now. The CI itself is real and running — scale is the gap, not the system.
No measured FARM-WIDE throughput or CI SLO at scale is claimed; single-crate + local cache/build/codegen figures are measured, farm-wide-at-scale is pending.
Concurrency figures beyond the measured local runs are design guidance, bounded by real provisioned capacity.
